title: the breath again — every claim checked
hook: the senses quarrel over who holds the body up, and breath settles it by getting up to leave
carry: the breath again — every claim checked

segments.voice: Last time, the breath again, with a promise attached: every claim checked. Today the checking begins.

An argument breaks out inside a body. Speech says it holds the body up. So does the mind. So do the eye and the ear. Each one is sure it's the pillar. Then breath, the quiet one, says nothing much. It just starts to leave. And the moment it lifts, every other power is dragged up with it, whether it likes it or not. This story sits in the second question of the Prashna Upanishad, a text built as six students asking a teacher six questions. Today: what it means by breath, and one popular claim, checked against the page.
screen: `AN ARGUMENT INSIDE A BODY.` → `BREATH STARTS TO LEAVE.` → `ONE CLAIM, CHECKED AGAINST THE PAGE.`

segments.voice: Here's the scene, in paraphrase. A student asks the teacher Pippalada which powers hold a being together, and which of them is greatest. The teacher tells the quarrel. The elements and the senses each claim the body. Breath warns them not to be fooled: it alone, dividing itself, keeps the body standing. They don't believe it. So breath rises to go, and they all rise with it. It settles, and they all settle, like bees following their king bee out of the hive and back again. Then the senses sing to breath, and the hymn makes it very large. Breath burns as fire, shines as the sun, falls as rain. Breath is in everything. Now the claim. You'll hear in wellness writing that prana is basically oxygen, or that it's a hidden energy a machine can read. The first is too small: the Prashna's breath is fire and rain and the life of creatures, not one gas in the lungs. The second is a different kind of claim altogether. The Upanishad never offers prana as something to measure. It offers a way of seeing a living thing as held together by something it doesn't control. So read prana as a teaching about life, not a reading on a dial. What a person can actually watch is the breath itself, going out and coming back. The Prashna asks for nothing more.
screen: `THE SENSES EACH CLAIM THE BODY` · `BEES FOLLOWING THEIR KING BEE` · `BREATH AS FIRE, SUN AND RAIN` · `A TEACHING, NOT A READING ON A DIAL`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and let the breath rise and settle without steering it. As it rises, notice what rises with it, the chest, the shoulders, maybe a thought; as it settles, let speech go quiet and the eyes rest, the swarm following its king bee. If you pray, you can offer one breath back with thanks.
The breath again. In the Prashna, breath gets up to leave and every other power rises with it, like bees with their king. Today's word.
Your line: the breath again — every claim checked. In the Prashna, breath is the one that holds the body up. See you tomorrow.
